items.title: Exclusive: Aina’s Smart Ring Wants to Be a Remote Control for Your AI Agent
items.excerpt: The startup Aina bets you won’t need to rely on your phone to control virtual assistants. It’s making a smart ring that lets you control the actions of your autonomous agents with one tap.
items.rationale: WIRED exclusive on a new one-tap agent-control ring; a different company and product from the Natura ring published 10-09.

items.title: Motorola Signature 27 gets Pixel's Gemini Intelligence features with Rambler, Create My Widget
items.excerpt: Motorola is adopting Google’s Gemini Intelligence features in the first major expansion beyond Pixel, with Gboard’s Rambler and more supported....
items.rationale: First time Pixel-only Gemini Intelligence features (Rambler, Create My Widget) reach another phone maker.

items.title: Samsung Android XR smart glasses pre-orders get started on November 12
items.excerpt: The smart glasses collaboration, featuring frames from Warby Parker and Gentle Monster, is about to start taking pre-orders.
items.rationale: Follow-up to the 10-14 reveal with a new concrete event: a fixed pre-order date for the Samsung/Warby Parker/Gentle Monster AI glasses.

items.title: Subvocal’s glasses promise to let you talk to your computer in complete silence
items.excerpt: Typing has always been a bottleneck between what we think and how quickly we can communicate it to a computer. AI-powered dictation tools like Wispr Flow have made things considerably better. You can practically ramble your way through an entire email, or even an article, and have it transcribed into text in seconds. But there’s […]
items.rationale: A new input approach: silent-speech glasses that feed AI dictation without speaking aloud; nothing like it in the 30-day history.

items.title: Gboard beta hints at a smarter Rambler that learns your words and contact names
items.excerpt: Gboard’s voice dictation feature, Rambler, may soon get a lot better by remembering contact names and corrected words.
items.rationale: Replacement pick: a concrete new capability for Gboard's AI dictation (it learns your corrected words and contact names), found in the current beta; it is about the keyboard itself, not Motorola's adoption of it.

https://www.androidauthority.com/samsung.new_action: Pre-orders for the Samsung Android XR glasses (Warby Parker / Gentle Monster frames) open on a set date, November 12

dedup.note: Swap 2026-11-06: removed Tom's Hardware 'npu-driver' pick. The enrichment fetch showed the NPU only does plain compositing, with no AI involved. Replacement: Android Authority Gboard Rambler teardown, which is new in the 30-day gadgets history (no Rambler story; the nearest is the 10-30 Raycast keyboard dictation card, a different product). It is distinct from the Motorola pick, which is about a phone maker adopting Pixel features, while this one is a new Rambler capability. Other candidates passed over: Moto Buds Ultra 27 (would be a second Motorola card, and its AI features are incidental), HomeView third-party chatbots (a code rumor close to the Verge 11-04 Siri third-party story), Notebookcheck robot study (possibly the same robot-safety research as zdnet.co.kr 10-25, with a cross-section risk for science), Android Auto Gemini bug (running story), SamMobile opinion, Verge Bee column (commentary), XDA/CNET how-tos, Engadget Warby Parker leak (same cluster as the Samsung pick), TechRadar Hue AI behaviors (likely repeat of 10-22). Outlets: WIRED, 9to5Google, Android Authority x2, Digital Trends (4 distinct, none over 2). Cross-section: published_urls.json is too large to read in full with Read-only tools, so I could not grep it. The replacement is a gadget-specific Gboard beta feature and unlikely to have run in another section.
